reuse.why: Reuses the shared eligibility predicate, tag parser, spreadsheet access and mutation wrappers, but setLastMonthSpending reimplements averageBudgetAmount.

duplication.why: The category-loading query is repeated across five actions, and the new spending action duplicates the existing income/expense sign conversion.

placement.why: Budget policy and calculations remain in actions.ts, while handler registration and undo integration follow app.ts conventions.

scope.why: Changes are confined to the requested month-wide actions, their registration and relevant tests.

maintainability.why: Eligibility rules remain centralized, but repeated queries, duplicated sign conversion and the now-unused action discriminator create avoidable maintenance work.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: setLastMonthSpending computes the income/expense sign locally instead of calling averageBudgetAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: setLastMonthSpending expresses averageBudgetAmount's sign conversion as `cat.is_income === 0 ? -spending : spending`.

abstraction_drift.where: shouldWriteMonthBudgetCategory gains includeHiddenCategories and guards for fixed groups and saved templates while retaining an unused action parameter; setLastMonthSpending bypasses averageBudgetAmount.
